questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to choose the best smart speaker for your home
Whether smart speakers listen to us, and why we use them
How governments protect our privacy with new laws
Why people don't answer phone calls from unknown numbers
questions.why: Dan says the topic is 'How safe is your smart speaker?'

questions.q: Why didn't Rob answer his phone at the start?
options: He didn't want Dan listening to his private call
He didn't hear it ring because of the music
He was angry with his wife after an argument
The battery was dead and it had switched off
questions.why: He says he's not crazy about someone eavesdropping on his phone call.

questions.q: How does Rob react when Dan asks how he knows his smart speaker isn't eavesdropping?
options: He says it's impossible
He says he switches it off at night
He realises he hadn't thought about it
He says he doesn't care
questions.why: Rob says, 'I see. I hadn't thought of that.'

questions.q: What does Florian Schaub say people are putting in their homes?
options: A camera that records everything they do all day
A robot that does housework while they are out
A device that secretly sells their data to shops
A listening device, in their most private space
questions.why: He says 'You're basically introducing... listening bug in your home.'

questions.q: What does Florian Schaub say about the microphone?
options: It is only on when you say the keyword
It is on all the time to detect the keyword
It can be removed easily
It doesn't work very well
questions.why: He says the microphone is still on the whole time in order to detect the keyword.

questions.q: What worry does Florian Schaub have about governments?
options: They might get around security to listen to people
They might ban smart speakers from being sold
They might put a high tax on smart speakers
They don't understand the technology well enough
questions.why: He says governments might try to circumvent security mechanisms to listen.

questions.q: According to Florian Schaub's study, how do many users feel about the privacy risk?
options: Very angry
Completely unaware of it
They accept it as the price of convenience
They plan to stop using speakers
questions.why: People are 'resigned to' the trade-off for the convenience the speaker provides.

questions.q: Why does Dan think the data smart speakers hear may not matter much?
options: Companies delete it immediately after using it
The speakers can't understand most people's accents
Most people don't talk much when they're at home
Companies already have lots of data about us anyway
questions.why: He says it's probably not significant 'considering all the data companies have about us already'.
